newsitem.title: USA: Montana wheat 98 pct harvested, weather stays dry.
newsitem.headline: Montana wheat 98 pct harvested, weather stays dry.

text.p: Montana's winter wheat harvest was nearly complete in the week ended Sunday, but extremely dry conditions raised the risk of brushfires, the Montana Agricultural Statistics Service said in its weekly update.
Winter wheat was 98 percent harvested as of Sunday against 92 percent a week ago, 73 a year ago and 77 on a five-year average.
Spring wheat was 81 percent harvested against the five-year average of 47 percent.
Barley was 72 percent harvested, ahead of the five-year average of 50 percent.
Soil moisture was rated 60 percent very short, 32 percent short, eight percent adequate and nil surplus.
Seven days were rated suitable for fieldwork and virtually no rainfall was recorded across eastern portions of the state.
"Extremely dry conditions continue," the report said. "Fire danger is critical in many areas of the state."
Pasture and range feed conditions were rated six percent very poor, 30 percent poor, 36 percent fair, 25 percent good and three percent excellent.
